verification.notes: Deviation classification is correct: as drafted the cap measured "Fees" (defined at §§ 1.5–1.6 as a one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) "under the first Order Form", which is far below 6 months' fees and sits in walk-away territory. The single operation cures that. Fallback is position-complete: mutuality, the 12-month fee basis, and the indemnity/confidentiality/gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct carve-outs are all present in operative language. Preferred is not complete. The only gap is the payment carve-out: § 21.3 excludes from "damages" only "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", and "Fees" remains the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee. To reach preferred, amend that sentence to read, e.g., "Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement is not damages and is not limited by this Section." The drafter's decision to leave it is defensible commercially but must not be described as preferred-complete. Minimality fails on the USD 1,000,000 floor. The declared target is the fallback, whose only numeric requirement is a cap "based on 12 months of fees"; "the greater of ... and (b) USD 1,000,000" exceeds that threshold with no stated necessity (and, because the cap is mutual, it also raises Customer's own exposure floor). Either delete "the greater of" and limb (b) to sit cleanly at the fallback, or keep the floor and pursue the full preferred level by also fixing the § 21.3 payment sentence. Minor drafting point (not a failure): the edit relies on lowercase "fees" to escape the capital-F defined term while §§ 1.5–1.6 are left intact. That is the right minimal move for the rest of the contract, but consider adding "(regardless of the definition of 'Fees' in Section 1.5)" or amending § 1.5 if Vendor argues the defined term controls. Intent is preserved: § 21.2's mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the direct-damages carve-in for data restoration and incident response, and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims definition are untouched; no cross-reference is left dangling and "Fees" remains defined for the payment and § 21.3 sentences.

Section 13.3 limits Vendor's ability to revoke or suspend to "a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure," which is the preferred uncured-material-breach-only standard for the subscription licence. Section 13.3 also permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, and Section 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor's consent, with Section 24.2 restricting Vendor-side assignment and Section 24.4 barring termination, suspension or repricing on Customer change of control. Transition obligations are triggered "[u]pon expiry or termination for any reason" (11.1); assistance runs for up to six months (well beyond the 90-day fallback) and is priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form, which is better for us than then-current rates; Customer Data is returned within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, and Vendor may not withhold it over a fee dispute (11.2); and an authorized officer certifies secure deletion only after Customer confirms successful return, with any law-required retained copy remaining protected and unusable for another purpose (11.3). Section 16 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so the exit mechanics operate post-termination. The only variations from preferred wording are that the 30-day return clock runs from Customer's request (a trigger we control, exercisable at or after termination) rather than automatically from termination, and the rate reference; neither is a material shortfall, so no redline is warranted.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Section 19 satisfies the warranty checklist at or above the fallback, and in substance reaches most of the preferred position. Services are warranted to be performed "in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards" with no time limitation, and Services and Deliverables are warranted to "materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications" (19.1). The hosted software (which is the "Services" under the definition in 1.8) is warranted to conform "throughout the subscription term", and Deliverables for ninety days after the later of delivery or acceptance (19.2) — comfortably beyond the 90-day software / 30-day services fallback floors. Section 19.4 supplies the required remedies: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, and, if Vendor cannot cure, termination of the affected item with a refund of Fees paid. Section 19.3 adds the preferred no-malicious-code and Applicable Law compliance warranties, and the disclaimer in 19.5 is expressly limited to implied warranties and states that "No disclaimer limits an express warranty", so it does not hollow out the express warranties. The only shortfall against the preferred wording is that the standalone Deliverable conformance period is 90 days rather than 12 months; Deliverables here are reports, configurations and similar work product rather than licensed software, and the hosted software is covered for the whole term, so this is noted rather than redlined. No redline proposed.

Clause 18.1 requires commercial general liability of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, professional E&O of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 (granted unconditionally, which more than satisfies the conditional preferred element given Vendor processes Customer Data under § 17).
